text:
Nikita Tolopilo had not played an NHL game all season. On Monday in Salt Lake City he faced 36 shots carrying almost six expected goals, allowed two, and walked out with a 3-2 win. The Mammoth did nearly everything you can do to win a hockey game except beat the goalie, and that left them winless in six (0-3-3).

The gap was enormous. Utah had 5.96 expected goals (the quality of its chances) to Vancouver's 3.03, 83 shot attempts to 52, and won the third period 2.49 to 0.99 in chance quality. Our replays of every shot give Utah this game 88% of the time. Tolopilo, never drafted and a .905 goalie in 35 AHL games with Abbotsford two seasons ago, saved 3.96 goals more than the shots deserved. "Some utter robberies," wrote Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis, and the biggest came with seconds left, a 42% chance from Kailer Yamamoto that would have sent the game to overtime.

The scoring went back and forth. Jake DeBrusk opened it on the power play late in the second. Vincent Trocheck tied it on a Utah power play 2:50 into the third, Filip Chytil restored the lead with a wraparound that had a 4% chance of going in, and Barrett Hayton tied it again at 11:39, a goal that lifted Utah from 18% to 52%. Then Brock Boeser, with a goal and two assists on the night, hammered a power-play slap shot at 15:37 that took Vancouver from 53% to 90%. The Canucks went 2 for 4 on the power play; that was their game.

For Vancouver, this follows a 6-3 win over Vegas that ended a seven-game losing streak, so a team that couldn't buy a result two weeks ago has two in a row. Boeser has been the driver ("Boesvember," per Wagner), but it is hard to call this one sustainable on the process. For Utah it is a different kind of hard. Logan Cooley returned for this game, while Dylan Guenther is out two to four weeks and Nick Schmaltz is hurt, and the team that showed up generated plenty. Karel Vejmelka allowed three on 2.76 expected, which won't quiet the questions KSL Sports raised after the San Jose loss. The process says Utah deserves better than six straight without a win. The standings don't grade process.
headline: Tolopilo steals one as Utah's skid reaches six
